title: How much of an open-source chip design search can cheap fidelity rungs and proof prediction save, with a guarantee?
lede: milestone 1 done: on 10 designs x 60 ABC pass sequences, the generic-gate score does not rank like routed SKY130 area x delay (tau-b median -0.04), and liberty mapping mis-ranks too when the clock is tight (tau 0.59); search and coverage hypotheses H2 to H5 not yet run
summary: An open research programme; milestone 1 is measured. Over 10 small designs, 60 ABC pass sequences each and two clock targets (1,200 runs through Yosys, ABC and OpenROAD on SKY130 HD), the generic-gate rung's Kendall tau-b against routed (global-route plus timing repair) area × period is below 0.7 on all 9 designs where it is defined (median −0.04), and its pick costs a median 13.5% of routed area × period. The liberty-mapped rung is no better than 0.59 median tau at a tight clock (median regret 10.5%) but nearly exact at a relaxed one (0% regret), because timing repair reorders designs. Routed points cost about 8× a generic point here, so there is little to save on designs this small. Limits: one corner and utilisation, global-route estimates, ten small designs. Hypotheses H2 to H5 (multi-fidelity wins, coverage, proof prediction) are not yet run.
